items.content:
A text survives if someone thought it worth the labour of copying, every
few generations, for two thousand years. Not once — continuously.

So what we have is not the best of antiquity. It is the most consistently
useful to institutions with scriptoria. Those overlap, but they are not
the same set, and we built a civilisation's idea of its own past on the
difference.

summary: What lasts is what institutions kept copying, not the best of antiquity
title: A note on what "survives" means
